items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Al Morgan come in. The first day he was there. Next day he was with the McKinney’s Cotton Pickers... Al Morgan and a couple of New Orleans . . . Zutty worked with him a while.

ctx.x: You had a lot of associations with New Orleans musicians up there.

There weren’t that many. The ones who were there, they were working with bands. I was the only one out there by myself. All the musicians was mad about New Orleans musicians, because they were innovators. Al Morgan come in. The first day he was there. Next day he was with the McKinney’s Cotton Pickers. From McKinney’s Cotton Pickers he went with Cab Calloway. All that in three months, because he played bass. They had never heard no bass player like that. They just were beginning to play the bass in 1930, because…

there was the Savoy. Then there was the Renaissance. Aw man, and there was a dozen others places with every element of black people. You get a chance to see all them people. West End the people hang out in one . . . certain bars. The black Cubans hang out in another bar. The Barbadans hang out in another. People from Virginia hang out in another bar. They had all that. People went to the source of their pleasures and their relations. What was that first question?

items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee mentions Al Morgan in a narrative about Cab Calloway and Keg Johnson ('And Al Morgan, who is from New Orleans, went to California...'), but does not describe a personal interaction or direct professional relationship with him.

ctx.x: Yeah. They used to go... Chris Kelly was going to play the weekend. He and Sam Morgan, they all went on the road. Every weekend they'd go to ..(?)..
Yes. Sam Morgan. There was four of them. Isaiah Morgan, Sam Morgan, Albert Morgan... There was five of them. They come down off the Magnolia Plantation, down in Magnolia, Louisiana, in ..(?)..(?)...

items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: Albert Morgan had come through and made a splash on the bass... They couldn't get to Braud... And he asked me, said, 'Man, that's a helluva bass. Have they got any more down there like that?'

ctx.x: Yes. Sam Morgan. There was four of them. Isaiah Morgan, Sam Morgan, Albert Morgan... There was five of them. They come down off the Magnolia Plantation, down in Magnolia, Louisiana, in ..(?)..(?)...
Did they all play bass? Were they all musicians?
